beginner.summary: For Python developers, data analysts and engineers who have used a neural network or an LLM chat tool but have never opened the machinery. Covers what a transformer is and how text becomes token IDs, embeddings, self-attention, multi-head attention, masks and the transformer block, then the Hugging Face transformers library: pipeline(), AutoTokenizer and AutoModel classes, config objects, reading logits and hidden states, generate(), chat templates, encoder embeddings, datasets and evaluate, devices and dtypes, plus vision and audio models. Ends with a capstone triage tool.
prerequisites: Writes Python functions and uses pip and virtual environments
Knows what a vector, matrix and matrix multiplication are, at the level of NumPy
Has a laptop or cloud notebook with 8 GB of RAM and Python 3.10 or later; a GPU is helpful but not required
outcomes: Explain, with shapes, how a transformer turns text into token IDs, attention weights and next-token probabilities
Implement scaled dot-product attention and a causal mask in PyTorch and match the output of torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention
Load tokenizers and models with the transformers Auto classes, run pipeline() and generate(), and read logits, hidden states and attention outputs
Build and evaluate a small multi-model text triage tool and document the limits of the pretrained models it uses
